name: Polish nationalism
summary: Polish nationalism holds that Poles form a nation whose culture, language, history and Catholic tradition deserve primacy and whose own sovereign state must guard its interests. Its classic form, Roman Dmowski's National Democracy, wanted an ethnically homogeneous Polish-speaking Catholic state, stressed national duty over individual and class interest, and treated minorities as to be Polonized or to leave. Its heirs today are national-conservative (Law and Justice) and far-right (Confederation) politics defending sovereignty, the family and national memory.
scope: Mainstream of the right-wing tradition: Dmowski's National Democracy (Thoughts of a Modern Pole, Church, Nation and State) as the canonical core, plus the contemporary national-conservative program of Law and Justice (2023 program) for modern questions. Excludes the earlier civic Commonwealth and Romantic messianic strands, Pilsudski's Jagiellonian federalism, and the monarchist and fascist-influenced fringes. Economic and social-policy answers are mostly low-confidence inferences, as the movement was defined by nation, state and religion rather than economics.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Dmowski wanted a business-minded modernizing Poland yet subordinated the economy to the nation; modern strands split between market liberals (Konfederacja) and state-minded conservatives.

public-ownership.rationale: Endecja gave no clear line on nationalization, and today's national-conservatives favor state control of strategic energy while market-oriented nationalists oppose it, so adherents are split.

unions-good.rationale: Nationalism opposed class-struggle unionism but Solidarity drew on nationalist currents; adherents are split and the sources do not settle it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Nationalists oppose speech laws that shield minorities yet favor laws protecting the nation's and Church's good name, so adherents split.

strong-leader.rationale: Dmowski deliberately backed a weak presidency and strong legislature against Pilsudski's strong-man style, while later nationalists admired authority; split.

state-harmful.rationale: Dmowski treated the state as the indispensable means by which the nation is constituted and guarded; the program calls the state the guarantor of national interest.

traditional-family.rationale: The program calls the family the fundamental social unit built on a lasting union of a woman and a man and pledges to defend and strengthen it.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The program defines marriage as man and woman and attacks ideologies aimed at undermining the family, which adherents apply against same-sex marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: The program states that killing unborn children is unacceptable, with exceptions only where the mother's life must be saved under existing legal grounds.

more-religion-public.rationale: Dmowski wrote that the Polish State is a Catholic State, and the PiS program places Catholicism at the center of Polish identity.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a Polish nationalist concern; the ideology rejects group-based remedies that put particular groups above the national whole.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The program rejects imposed ideologies that dissolve natural categories like family and nation; adherents reject the social-construction view of gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The program defines the nation as a community of culture, language and history and rejects efforts to dissolve it; cultural preservation is core.

gradual-change.rationale: Dmowski criticized romantic uprisings in favor of pragmatic, peaceful politics and the ND pursued its aims by parliamentary means.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The program rejects erosion of state sovereignty and wants a union of sovereign nations, which runs against empowering supranational bodies.

free-trade.rationale: No stated doctrine; Dmowski favored a strong national economy but modern nationalists range from free-market to protectionist.

nation-first.rationale: Dmowski's concept of healthy national egoism makes the nation the absolute object of moral obligation and its interest the criterion in foreign relations.

open-borders.rationale: Open borders contradict the homogeneous nation-state goal central to National Democracy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Dmowski valued science and modernization but the ideology makes no progress-through-technology claim.

revolution-justified.rationale: National Democrats advocated negotiation, not armed resistance, and Dmowski opposed romantic insurrection, though later memory celebrates anti-communist fighters.

experts-over-public.rationale: Dmowski valued disciplined elites yet appealed to the national mass; genuinely mixed.

central-planning.rationale: Dmowski rejected socialism as placing class above the nation; central planning was associated with the communist order nationalists fought.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The family-centered program favors protecting family continuity, so heavy inheritance taxes are disfavored.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism favors protecting domestic industry, though the sources opened do not state it.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Rejection of socialism and Marxist class doctrine leaves no room for abolishing wages.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Some interwar nationalist currents leaned corporatist after radicalizing but Endecja mainly worked within parliament; split.

one-party-rule.rationale: The National Democrats pursued their aims through democratic and parliamentary means and opposed the Sanacja regime.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Dmowski's movement was republican and parliamentary, while a monarchist wing split under Braun; mainstream is not monarchist.

democracy-best.rationale: Dmowski valued mass politics for forming nations yet objected to parliamentarianism and liberal democracy placing the individual first; split.

direct-votes.rationale: The sources describe Endecja working through parliament and nothing on referendums; modern nationalist parties differ on direct democracy, so adherents split.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as basis of political power are a socialist institution that Dmowski opposed.

right-to-secede.rationale: The goal of a unified homogeneous nation-state and Polonization of border regions contradicts a right to secede.

natural-rulers.rationale: Social Darwinist hierarchy of strong and weak nations is stated, but a doctrine of natural rulers within the nation is not.

political-violence-never.rationale: National Democrats preferred peaceful negotiation but the movement's later boycotts and attacks and the cult of anti-communist fighters show it is not absolute.

separate-church-state.rationale: Dmowski declared the Polish state Catholic and held Catholicism integral to Polishness, so strict separation is rejected.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Catholicism is integral to the nation but Dmowski's ethics are national rather than scriptural law; adherents want Christian values in law, not scripture as law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state is indispensable to the nation, so privatized defense and justice are rejected.

ethnic-nation.rationale: National Democracy aimed at an ethnically homogeneous Polish-speaking Catholic state, rejecting the multiethnic Commonwealth model.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Dmowski rejected class as an organizing principle and saw history as struggle between nations.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rejects socialism and egalitarian class politics in favor of the nation's organic hierarchy.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The nation's own historical claims are against Germany and Russia; general colonial reparations are not part of the program.

civilizational-union.rationale: Dmowski built nationalism on distinct nations, not supranational civilizational unions, though Catholic Europe is valued.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Dmowski held individual egoism to be an immoral element of human nature that national duty must restrain; only national egoism is valued.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Dmowski taught that an individual is a debtor to the nation and has duties to repay, making duty primary.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: None of the sources opened takes a stance on the intrinsic value of nature, and nationalist thought centers on the nation rather than ecology.

limit-population.rationale: Program emphasizes boosting births and honoring parenthood; limits are disfavored.

restore-past-order.rationale: Dmowski attacked romantic backward-looking nationalism, while later nationalists invoke a lost tradition; split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Dmowski urged pragmatic politics aimed at national results over romantic gestures, a position the Dmowski article documents.

direct-action.rationale: ND stressed parliamentary and peaceful methods; boycotts were used but not as anti-electoral doctrine.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources are silent on whether methods must mirror aims; Dmowski's realism stresses effectiveness, but nothing stated either way.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: This is a Marxist utopian goal; Dmowski rejected socialism and class doctrines, so adherents disagree.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Dmowski rejected Marxist class analysis and promoted class collaboration within the nation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Polish nationalists defined themselves against communism and Soviet rule, and Dmowski rejected class dominance over the nation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Dmowski explained international conflict by struggle between nations, not by the economic system, so this Leninist claim is rejected.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state is the necessary instrument of the nation, so taxation is legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: Dmowski subordinated individual conduct to national moral duty, so adherents accept more state restriction than the harm principle allows.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Dmowski held the nation, not the individual, to be the subject of moral obligations; rights are not only individual.

conscription.rationale: National duty and the debt of individuals to the nation make compulsory defense service acceptable.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Nation binding makes exit-as-check unattractive; the nation is the individual's primary community.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Dmowski used racial and organic language yet Majka argues he did not base worth on biology; sources are mixed.

organic-representation.rationale: Dmowski saw nation as a living organism but did not call for corporate representation in place of parties.

total-state.rationale: The movement's central value is the nation, not an all-directing state; the program defends a sovereign but not totalitarian state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Nationalists see a revival of national consciousness as the answer to partition-era weakness, though Dmowski opposed romantic messianism.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Dmowski sought broader borders for Poland, while modern adherents accept present borders; split.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is contrary to a mass modern nation; Dmowski criticized noble privileges.

universal-morality.rationale: Dmowski's national ethics have no basis in natural law and are relative to each nation, though Christian ethics govern individuals.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: National Democracy favored Jewish emigration while modern Polish right supports Israel; split.

revive-national-language.rationale: Culture and language are foundations of the nation, so revival is favored though Polish never fell out of use.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: No stated position; PiS governed with large deficits yet nationalist market liberals disagree.

economic-freedom.rationale: The sources do not link political and economic freedom; market-oriented nationalists such as Konfederacja agree while state-minded national-conservatives do not.

national-self-determination.rationale: Polish nationalism arose to restore an independent Polish state and nation-state autonomy.

force-without-un.rationale: Sources are silent on UN authorization; sovereignty-minded nationalists distrust the UN while Poland relies on alliances for legitimacy, so split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Dmowski held patriotism to be instinct stronger than reasoning and embraced Catholicism.

class-collaboration.rationale: Dmowski rejected class struggle as placing class above the nation and proposed cooperation of all classes within the national whole.

dominated-front.rationale: Polish nationalists distrust Russia but align with the West; no such front.

workers-nation.rationale: Dmowski put the nation above class and the movement sought workers within a national frame.

ban-interest.rationale: Nothing in the opened sources supports a legal ban on interest; Polish nationalism has no usury doctrine, so the answer is a low-confidence disagreement.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Dmowski rejected Marxist class theory and saw the state as the instrument by which the nation is constituted, not a ruling-class tool.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Endecja promoted Polonization of minorities, implying assimilation expectation.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory some Polish far-right adherents voice, not a documented core claim.

proportional-representation.rationale: The ND worked within a parliament but no stated position on electoral system.

national-mission.rationale: Dmowski's positivists rejected romantic Messianism as a basis of policy; spreading a political form abroad is not a program.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The program defends the traditional family and attacks ideological critiques of family and gender, so adherents reject the claim that society systematically advantages men.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Dmowski treated some foreign blood as improving the nation; ethnic exclusivism toward Jews existed but not a racial mixing ban.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: National Democracy sought exclusion of Jews from parts of national life, rejecting equal civil standing.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: With Catholicism central to Polish identity per the program and Dmowski, adherents expect religious instruction in state schools.

population-transfer.rationale: Dmowski sought minorities polonized or removed and National Democrat Grabski shaped postwar population shifts.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: National struggle doctrine makes absolute pacifist-libertarian rule unacceptable.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Dmowski's social Darwinism saw international life as a struggle between strong and weak nations, making competition formative for peoples.

separated-powers.rationale: Dmowski favored a strong legislature to check executive power in the 1921 constitution.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist doctrine; Polish nationalism opposes communism and works through national parties and parliament.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Catholic social teaching might favor it, yet the opened sources give no nationalist position on prioritizing the poor.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The program treats births as national strength and honors parenthood, which contradicts blaming population growth for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Dmowski saw minorities as threats to national cohesion and wanted a homogeneous nation.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Lottery selection is alien to nationalist politics, which favors representation of the nation through parties and leaders.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Interwar nationalists opposed Sanacja repression but accepted harsh measures in principle; split.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: PiS notably lifts party discipline on worldview questions but nationalist parties differ.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The program says it does not accept erosion of European states' sovereignty and wants a Europe of fatherlands rather than deeper pooling.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Dmowski backed a weak presidency and strong legislature to limit Pilsudski.

clerical-rule.rationale: Catholicism is integral but Dmowski's national ethics put the nation, not clergy, in command.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Duty to the nation comes first, so supporting the state in war is expected.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Dmowski wanted a weak presidency, and Polish nationalists distrust personal rule; the sources state no term-limit view.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Polish nationalists historically sought allies against Germany and Russia and remain alliance-oriented.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Partitions divided the Polish nation among three empires and unification was the central aim.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist right themes include distrust of educated elites, but sources do not document it as a core nationalist claim.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Dmowski's social Darwinism ranks nations as strong and weak and places Catholic Polish culture first.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The program attacks ideologies aimed at the family; adherents oppose gender-equality curricula.

minority-language-support.rationale: Endecja sought Polonization and opposed the Minority Rights Treaty, so state support for minority languages is rejected.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Nation over individualism; Dmowski warns about undisciplined individualism.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: National interest first; Dmowski rejects humanity as a subject of obligations.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Dmowski favored a weak president chosen by parliament in 1921, but modern nationalists accept popular election; split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Polish irredentist memory of the Kresy keeps attachment to historic land alive, so adherents resist trading territory; low confidence.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The program recalls German and Soviet occupation and annexation of Polish lands, which supports treating annexed territory as occupied.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Catholic State position and central place of the Church in the program contradict subordinating it to the state.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Nationalists favored parliament and the constitution against Pilsudski's personal rule, so a ruler above law is rejected.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The sources record no stance on mixed constitutions in the classical sense; neutral.

refugee-return.rationale: Nationalist postwar thinking favored population shifts such as expulsion of Germans.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Polish irredentism keeps the memory of the Kresy and Dmowski claimed territory where Poles lived; modern states accept borders, so low confidence.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Endecja favored Polonization and opposed the Minority Rights Treaty, so self-governing minority institutions are rejected.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: National Democrats pushed for Jewish emigration rather than equal rights where they lived, according to the National Democracy article.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender parity quotas belong to the gender ideologies that the program rejects; adherents disagree.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: National Democrats advocated peaceful negotiation over armed uprising, per the National Democracy article.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Dmowski attacked the noble privileges of the old Commonwealth in Thoughts of a Modern Pole.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nationalist narratives center history on the Polish nation and the program recounts national history as central to identity.

patriotic-education.rationale: Dmowski called patriotism a moral duty to the nation, and the program stresses national history and memory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Memory of the Kresy supports influence in the east, while Dmowski opposed Pilsudski's eastern federation plan; split.

elective-rulers.rationale: Early Polish protonationalism was tied to the republican szlachta tradition with elective kings, per the Polish nationalism article.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Golden Freedoms tradition of the Commonwealth allowed resistance to unlawful kings, which early nationalism inherited.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Dmowski backed a strong legislature in the 1921 constitution against Pilsudski.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Dmowski taught that individuals owe active duty to the nation, so withdrawal is rejected.

party-own-road.rationale: Polish nationalists oppose Soviet direction of Poland but take no stance on communist party autonomy.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Nationalists value self-reliance but accept alliances and EU funds; sources do not decide.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Kresy memory exists but the modern movement accepts present borders; split.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The program highlights resistance to German and Soviet occupation, but nationalists dislike anti-fascism as a constitutional doctrine; split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The program recounts German and Soviet occupation as parallel disasters and the modern history policy condemns both together.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Polish nationalism has no stake in the American Civil War; low confidence disagreement from mainstream history.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Poland removed communist monuments, yet nationalists defend their own national heroes despite criticism; split.

single-official-language.rationale: National Democrats pursued Polonization of minorities in the Kresy and elsewhere, favoring Polish as the sole common language.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The program condemns Soviet domination of Poland, which included intervention to keep bloc members in line.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The program pledges to protect parenthood and honor motherhood, supporting state incentives for births.

non-intervention.rationale: The sovereignty emphasis of the program favors non-interference, though Poland supports allies against Russia; low.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Split: Dmowski asserted an international Jewish conspiracy and the National Democrats spread it, but modern mainstream strands disavow it.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The program defends marriage as a lasting union of woman and man with state support, so abolition is rejected.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The program does not accept erosion of state sovereignty, implying national constitutional primacy.

religious-nation.rationale: Dmowski wrote that the Polish state is Catholic and held Catholicism integral to Polishness.

defeat-communism.rationale: The program praises anti-communist resistance and Dmowski's nationalism defined itself against socialism.

religion-illusion.rationale: Dmowski embraced Catholicism as integral to Polish identity, so the view that religion is an illusion is rejected.

socialized-care.rationale: The program makes family the fundamental unit and honors motherhood, so adherents oppose shifting housework and childcare to public services.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Dmowski rejected socialism but did not offer a third way as a defining doctrine; neutral.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The family-centered program is hostile to LGBT claims but Poland decriminalized long ago and the opened sources do not support criminalization; low.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The program rejects ideologies that dissolve the nation and family, so adherents reject intersectional analysis.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The program rejects ideological constructs on gender and defends the traditional family; adherents oppose legal recognition.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: A nationalist movement formed around national struggle and the army tradition rejects abolishing the armed forces.

domination-women-nature.rationale: This ecofeminist thesis belongs to the gender ideologies the program rejects, and the program's family-centered view of women's role does not link it to domination of nature.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A Marxist critique of liberal freedoms; nationalists do not frame press freedom this way.

racial-franchise.rationale: National Democrats worked in a parliament open to all citizens, even as they sought minority exclusion; the opened sources do not support voting by group.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: National Democrats organized boycotts of Jewish-owned shops in the 1930s, according to the National Democracy article.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: State atheism was the policy of communist rule that nationalists resisted, and Catholicism is integral to their identity.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Church charity is valued in the Catholic outlook, but the program supports family benefits from the state; low.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The program speaks of woman and man in lasting union and modern Catholic Poland accepts spousal partnership; low.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Radical wings of the movement used youth organizing but mainstream Endecja did not make drilled youth movements central; split.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The PiS-era mainstream seeks allied and especially American troops, though some nationalists object; low.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: This is a socialist or Georgist claim; nationalists lack a position on it.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: National Democracy focused on economic competition from Jews and urged boycotts and exclusion from parts of economic life.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: National Democracy held that national struggle and defence are a duty, and the national-conservative mainstream accepts armed defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The PiS programme stresses national memory and tradition running from the Polish state's origins to today.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The national-conservative programme defends the traditional family and fixed sex roles and opposes gender ideology.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Defence of the traditional family and its roles assumes a stable category of women.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Polish national memory honours those who died for Poland as martyrs, and PiS politics of memory gives this a central place.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Dmowski rejected socialism outright, but the question of what counts as socialism was not one the movement debated; neutral inference.

person-over-state.rationale: Dmowski made the nation the object of moral duty, with the individual subordinate to it, and rejected liberal individualism.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The movement identifies Polishness with Catholicism and treats religion as part of the national moral order, and the PiS programme defends the Church and Christian values.

racial-pride.rationale: Strong national pride is central, but pride in race as such is not the movement's idiom; adherents would be split on the wording.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Dmowski's national egoism did not rule out force for national aims, while today's heirs stress defence; split, so neutral.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Dmowski's National Democracy defined the nation by Polish language, culture and Catholic tradition, so shared language and history are central, though it added religion and ethnicity that the statement sets aside.

communal-electorates.rationale: National Democracy wanted a homogeneous Polish state in which minorities are Polonized or leave, so separate electorates for religious communities run against it.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Poland's history of partition and occupation, which the PiS program recalls, makes suspicion of German and Russian designs a recurring theme of national-conservative politics.

free-public-college.rationale: Public universities already charge no tuition for full-time students in Poland, and the sources do not show the movement taking a side; left as split.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Dmowski stressed national duty above individual conscience, and PiS-era politics reveres the military, so refusing orders is rejected.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Endecja stressed national over class interest and PiS is pro-worker but not committed to sectoral bargaining; adherents are split, and the sources are silent.

smash-state-machine.rationale: National Democracy sought a strong Polish state under national leadership and PiS works through existing institutions; revolutionary destruction of the state is alien to it.

sacred-nation.rationale: Dmowski placed the nation above the individual as an enduring moral community with religious roots, and PiS programmes speak of the nation as a lasting spiritual heritage.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Dmowski's ethics and Catholic-conservative thought treat human nature as fixed and the source of moral duties, though Dmowski ranked national over universal rights.

public-service-media.rationale: PiS-era policy brought public broadcasting under government influence and framed it as a national-interest institution, not independent of the government.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Dmowski rejected liberalism and put the nation's interest above individual rights and procedures, so elections alone would not make a state legitimate.

premarital-sex.rationale: The Catholic identification of the tradition and the PiS programme's defence of family and marriage support traditional sexual morality.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The tradition identifies the nation with the Catholic Church and PiS defends its teaching on family and abortion, so it rejects the view that religion oppresses women.

race-social-construct.rationale: Dmowski's national anthropology treated nations as natural wholes with real differences, so adherents lean against calling these categories mere constructs.

defend-planned-state.rationale: National Democracy saw socialism as a threat to national unity, so defending a planned state is not its position.

national-church-status.rationale: Dmowski made Catholicism part of Polish national identity and the PiS programme defends it, which supports special standing for the church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: National Democracy wanted a homogeneous Polish state and Polonization of minorities, which excludes ethnic territorial autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Adherents are split; Poland's own border claims favoured plebiscites in some areas and not in others.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about defending or claiming the homeland, not a spiritual bond with it, which is all the statement now asks about.

reviewHistory.rationale: Dmowski made the nation an object of moral duty, and PiS's programme stresses the history of occupation and defending Polish land.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about defending or claiming the homeland, not a spiritual bond with it, which is all the statement now asks about.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

self-ownership.rationale: Dmowski put national duty above individual interest, and PiS's programme restricts abortion, so full individual rights over one's body are rejected.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Dmowski's National Democrats worked through parliamentary methods and favoured a strong legislature.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: National Democracy identified the Polish nation with Catholicism and PiS's programme links nation, family and Church, so politics organised around Catholic identity is accepted.

material-over-identity.rationale: Adherents are split: they dislike identity politics of the left but themselves put national and religious identity first.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Dmowski rejected socialism and liberalism alike, and the tradition is strongly anti-communist, so a communist-led system is opposed.

missingStatements.text: Universities should limit the share of students from particular ethnic or religious minorities.
missingStatements.rationale: Dmowski backed a numerus clausus and cultural exclusion of Jews, a recurring National Democratic demand.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow discriminatory policy tied to interwar Poland; boycott-minority-shops and assimilate-immigrants already capture the exclusionary stance.

missingStatements.text: A country's economic life should be in the hands of members of the national majority rather than of minority groups.
missingStatements.rationale: National Democracy focused on economic competition from Jews and urged boycotts and exclusion from parts of economic life.

notes: Statements on minorities and Jews reflect Dmowski's National Democracy and interwar Endecja; contemporary mainstream national-conservatives disavow some of them. Economic answers are mostly inferred: the movement spans market-liberal (Confederation) and statist-welfarist (Law and Justice) positions.
